Pipeline stage: item review

Source: R/pipeline-review.R
review_packet.Rd

Items, whether written by people or generated, need human content and sensitivity (bias) review before they are field-tested. review_packet() writes a review form (a CSV file that opens in a spreadsheet) with one row per item and reviewer, ready for reviewers to fill in. read_reviews() reads their decisions back, sets each item's status ("approved", "revise" or "rejected", by majority) and runs the review checks.

Usage

review_packet(
  p,
  file = "review-packet.csv",
  reviewers = NULL,
  ai_screen = FALSE,
  provider = NULL,
  model = NULL
)

read_reviews(p, reviews)

Arguments

p

a pipeline with items from generate_items() or add_items().

file

path of the CSV file to write.

reviewers

optional reviewer names; the packet then has one row per item and reviewer.

ai_screen

logical; screen items with a language model first.

provider, model

the language model for the screen.

reviews

the completed packet: a path to the CSV file or a data frame with columns id, reviewer, decision (accept, revise or reject), aligned (yes/no), sensitivity (yes/no) and optionally comment. Rows with an empty decision are ignored.

Value

review_packet() returns the pipeline (with the screen's notes in p$items$ai_screen) invisibly and writes file.

read_reviews() returns the pipeline with the reviews in p$reviews, an agreement summary in p$review_agreement, and the items' status updated.

Details

With ai_screen = TRUE, a language model (see mv_ask_setup()) first screens every item for possible bias, sensitivity and accessibility problems; its notes go into the packet for reviewers to weigh. The screen assists reviewers and does not replace them.

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • under_reviewed (block): an item reviewed by fewer than min_reviewers reviewers.

  • alignment (review): a reviewer does not agree the item measures its blueprint cell.

  • sensitivity (review): a reviewer (or the AI screen) raised a bias or sensitivity concern.

  • needs_revision (review): reviewers asked for the item to be revised.

  • reviewer_agreement (info): Fleiss' kappa for the reviewers' decisions is below review_kappa.

  • provenance (info): an item without a recorded source (person or model), which testing programs now need to disclose.

Examples

items <- data.frame(stem = c("2 + 2 = ?", "3 x 3 = ?"), A = c("4", "6"),
                    B = c("5", "9"), key = c("A", "B"), cell = "Arithmetic")
p <- add_items(mv_pipeline(verbose = FALSE), items)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
p <- review_packet(p, f, reviewers = c("Ana", "Ben"))
rv <- utils::read.csv(f)
rv$decision <- "accept"; rv$aligned <- "yes"; rv$sensitivity <- "no"
p <- read_reviews(p, rv)
p$items$status
#> [1] "approved" "approved"
